page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance allocates a single dedicated x86_64 core running on an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor at a 5.0 GHz clock frequency without hyperthreading. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates modern instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA-NI. The host configuration pairs this single core with 4.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.

The instance does not bundle any local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent file system operations. Networking is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is absent, routing all graphics, mathematical, and vector processing through the AMD CPU.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a pronounced contrast between single-threaded velocity and overall parallel capacity. Driven by the 5.0 GHz AMD EPYC core, the instance scores in the top tier on single-core workloads, registering 4180.09 in stress-ng single-core tests and 3084.0 in Geekbench single-core metrics. Single-threaded data handling is notably fast, posting 45.72 GB/sec in gzip compression and 20.29 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance is limited to a single physical core, multi-core metrics such as Geekbench multi-core (3068.0) and parallel compilation tests fall into the lower quartile. Large-block uncached memory operations reach 49.14 GB/sec read and 43.72 GB/sec write bandwidth.

Given its architectural balance, m8azn.medium provides resource efficiency for workloads bottlenecked by raw clock speed rather than thread parallelism. The configuration aligns with lightweight microservices, static web content distribution (delivering 7.53 GB/sec in throughput testing), automated build agents, and small single-threaded data manipulation tasks. Highly concurrent web servers, heavy database engines, and parallel compute jobs will require larger multi-core instances.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor. It features a single dedicated x86_64 physical core running at 5.0 GHz, supported by 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz. The instance includes AVX-512 vector support and cryptographic acceleration, but omits local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external EBS volumes and offering a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute, text processing, and compression capability, balanced against weak multi-core throughput due to the single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth reaches 49.14 GB/sec for uncached large reads. This hardware profile makes m8azn.medium an efficient choice for lightweight microservices, static web delivery, continuous integration tasks, and applications requiring high clock frequencies without multi-threaded concurrency.
